material_class.structural_family: enneanuclear Cu5Gd4 cluster of vertex- and face-sharing {GdCu3} tetrahedra (Cu5 bow-tie plus Gd4 rectangle)

synthesis.procedure: Cu(NO3)2·3H2O (0.2 g, 1 mmol) was dissolved in 20 ml of MeOH, followed by addition of triethanolamine (0.13 ml, 1 mmol), pivalic acid (0.05 g, 0.5 mmol) and triethylamine (0.5 ml, 3.5 mmol) to give a green/blue solution. Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.45 g, 1 mmol) was then added to give a deep blue solution. The mixture was stirred for 4 h, allowed to stand, and layered with diethyl ether. After 3–4 days, blue crystals of 1 had formed.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction in methanol followed by diethyl ether layering
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: After stirring, the solution was allowed to stand and layered with diethyl ether; blue crystals formed after 3–4 days.

properties.summary: DC susceptibility of the isotropic Cu5Gd4 cluster shows dominant ferromagnetic pathways, a low-T net spin approaching S = 31/2, and many low-lying spin states. Combined magnetisation and heat-capacity data give a record molecular magnetocaloric effect, with −ΔSm reaching 31 J kg−1 K−1 at 3 K for ΔB0 = 9 T and large ΔTad (cooling rates >1 K T−1 at 9 T and >2 K T−1 at 1 T), making 1 an efficient refrigerant in the liquid-helium range.

measurements.conditions: B0 = 0.01 T; 2–300 K DC susceptibility; nearly constant down to ~30 K

measurements.name: magnetisation saturation
measurements.conditions: T = 2 K; consistent with net spin S = 31/2
